goals.0: The most common way to talk about the past: Perfekt
goals.2: The verb in second place, the Partizip at the end
goals.3: Time words: yesterday, the day before yesterday, last week
dialog.0.de.6.n: Partizip II: ge + mach + t. It goes to the end of the sentence
dialog.2.de.5.n: arbeiten → gearbeitet (an e is added before the t)
dialog.4.de.5.n: besuchen → besucht: no ge- after the prefix be-
grammar.0.title: Perfekt = haben (second place) + Partizip II (end)
grammar.0.text: In spoken German, the Perfekt is the most common way to talk about the past. haben goes in second place and Partizip II goes right at the end — like the verb at the end of a Bangla sentence (“shikhechi”).
grammar.1.title: Regular verbs: ge- + stem + -t
grammar.1.note: Verbs starting with be-, ver-, ent-, er- take no ge- (besucht, bezahlt). If the stem ends in t or d, add -et: gearbeitet.
grammar.2.title: Time words for the past
quiz.5.prompt: What is the Partizip II of arbeiten?
quiz.5.why: The stem ends in t → ge…et: gearbeitet.
quiz.6.prompt: What is the Partizip II of besuchen?
quiz.6.why: Verbs starting with be- take no ge-.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order: “Yesterday I learned German.”
quiz.7.why: haben in second place, Partizip at the end.
